title: The Little Elder-Tree Mother (The Dryad's Song)
summary: From the fragrant blossom of an elder tree sprang the gentle spirit of remembrance, folding the sick boy within the sheltering boughs of family affection....
full_text:
From the fragrant blossom of an elder tree sprang the gentle spirit of remembrance, folding the sick boy within the sheltering boughs of family affection.

Through her eyes, he beheld the sacred passage of ordinary human life: the youth who planted an acorn, the lovers who exchanged simple rings of iron, the mother who nursed her sick child by candlelight, and the venerable elders who sat upon the garden bench under the golden leaves of autumn, their hands intertwined in fifty years of unwavering fidelity.

"True poetry," whispered the Elder-Tree Mother, "is not found in marble palaces, but in the fidelity of hearts that beat for one another in simplicity and honor."

When the vision dissolved, the boy arose refreshed and whole, holding in his hand the everlasting blossom of gratitude.
moral: Faithful love shared through the storms of life ripens into a peaceful autumn of blessed remembrance.
